threads.body: A JSON request whose `inferenceConfig.topP` is an integer such as `10**400` now raises `OverflowError` in `_safe_float`. Extraction runs before the SDK call and its error handler, so this prevents the call and leaves the invocation unfinished. Add `OverflowError` to `_safe_float`'s exception tuple and add a public-client regression test that verifies the SDK's error still propagates.

inferenceConfig accepts snake_case aliases (max_new_tokens, top_p, top_k, stop_sequences) in addition to the camelCase keys documented in the Converse-aligned schema

The documented API references only the camel case ones though https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_InferenceConfiguration.html . We can take a look at converse in a followup PR though

threads.body: The new regression checks only synchronous, non-streaming success with content capture disabled, leaving Nova's four request settings unverified on the other supported paths. Extend public-client tests to async `invoke_model` and sync/async `invoke_model_with_response_stream`, including provider errors, early stream closure, and content capture enabled. Assert the exact four settings on finalized spans and absent message content when capture is disabled, as required by the [instrumentation test rules](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/blob/main/instrumentation/AGENTS.md#tests).
